source.title: Repetition over Diversity: High-Signal Data Filtering for Sample-Efficient German Language Modeling
source.authors: Ansar Aynetdinov; Patrick Haller; Alan Akbik

record.file_problem: none; the full paper, references, and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across parameter counts, token budgets, and training-data regimes in German language modeling, extending the scale-performance question to a non-English setting. It does not reproduce the original held-out-loss scaling measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream benchmark and instruction-tuning outcomes, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fitted power laws, extrapolation from small runs, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It cites scaling-law research but does not test those claims. Rows record the reported aggregate benchmark outcomes and aggregate judge metrics; external reference-model results are not included as study-trained scale conditions.
record.test_reason: A data-filtering study for German LMs. A small part bears on V6: it reports downstream benchmark and instruction-tuned judge scores at 350M vs 1B parameters and at 100B vs 200B tokens. That is only two points per axis. No loss is measured, no curve is fitted and nothing is extrapolated, so only the direction of V6 (downstream improves with scale) is tested, not its predictability. Most rows compare data subsets at fixed scale and do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that multi-epoch training on strictly filtered German subsets beats single-pass training on larger, less-filtered data at 350M and 1B parameters and 100–200B tokens. Gains persist to 7.2 epochs and through instruction tuning. They note the work does not establish generalization to other languages or to larger scales.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains models from scratch on different filtered/repeated data subsets and measures downstream benchmark and instruction-tuning scores. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy or fit power laws as in the original scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream results depend on data subset and training schedule; the authors report poorer outcomes for AA HIGH than for the denser subsets and different gains across RANDOM, DENSE-CORE, and PHASED conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed parameters and tokens, the pretraining data subset shifts downstream scores by up to ~5 points (RANDOM 34.35 vs DENSE-CORE 39.24). After instruction tuning, 350M DENSE-CORE at 200B tokens outscores 1B RANDOM at 100B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining data quality changes downstream performance at fixed scale by amounts comparable to a ~3x increase in parameters.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: For the claim's scaling-law components, the study does not report held-out pretraining loss, fit exponents, compute-optimal allocations, or predictive extrapolations. Its model scale is limited to 350M and 1B parameters and up to 200B tokens; results are for German. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the aggregate outcomes. Judge metrics are aggregates across three judges, with per-judge breakdowns elsewhere in the paper.
record.rows_left_out: Per-benchmark decompositions for the aggregate scores in Tables 3, 8, and 9 are not separately catalogued; per-judge breakdowns in Tables 10 and 11 are also omitted. External reference-model benchmark scores (Tables 3–5) are excluded because they are comparisons to models trained elsewhere, not study-run scaling conditions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits and no extrapolation to larger runs.
Architecture shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
Repeated-data training (up to 7.2 epochs) is studied only through downstream scores; no power-law form is tested.
No exponents are fitted, so fit-dependence is not examined.
Predictability is untested: there is no fitted relation, there are only two points per scale axis, and downstream scores are not related to pretraining loss.

missing.what: Downstream benchmark scores over pretraining checkpoints (performance vs tokens seen) for each subset, relevant to token scaling of downstream performance
Per-benchmark breakdowns of the 350M→1B and 100B→200B changes; e.g. MMLU barely moves for RANDOM with tokens (27.13→26.82)

record.verdict_notes: The study is mainly about data quality versus repetition; its link to scaling laws is incidental and limited to two-point scale comparisons of downstream scores. The original record linked every row to V6, including fixed-scale data comparisons; those are relinked to none. There are internal inconsistencies for PHASED: 37.64 vs 37.92 at 100B, and 1.6x vs 2.6x repetition at 200B. No uncertainty estimates and single seeds.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss is reported as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute; no power-law fit is made.
No small-run loss fit or prediction of larger-run loss is reported.
No loss-minimizing parameter/token split is selected or fitted at fixed compute.
Architecture is not varied at fixed parameter count to measure its effect on loss.
Repeated-data training is studied for downstream performance, but no power-law form in held-out loss is tested; no other modality is studied.

The paper compares downstream scores across selected German model sizes, token budgets, and data conditions, but does not fit or evaluate a predictive scaling relation or relate downstream performance to pretraining loss.
No scaling exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted, and no dependence of these fits on setup or fitting choices is tested.

relationships.condition: Parameter scaling 350M→1B at 100B tokens (RANDOM and DENSE-CORE), and token doubling 100B→200B for DENSE-CORE and PHASED at 350M and for DENSE-CORE at 1B
relationships.reason: Benchmark averages rise: 34.35→36.83 and 39.24→41.97 with parameters; 39.24→40.16, 37.92→39.07 and 41.97→44.05 with tokens. Judge scores also rise (T3-14, T3-16, T3-11, T3-12, T3-17, T3-37–T3-47). Direction only; nothing is fitted.
relationships.display_finding: Benchmark averages rose from 34.35 to 36.83 and 39.24 to 41.97 with parameter scaling, and from 39.24 to 40.16, 37.92 to 39.07 and 41.97 to 44.05 with token doubling, while judge scores also improved.

relationships.condition: Single-pass RANDOM data, 350M, token budget doubled 100B→200B
relationships.reason: The benchmark gain is only +0.40 (34.35→34.75), the final 200B checkpoint scores below the 197B one, and Likert rises only 3.11→3.34. Token-scaling gains depend on data quality (T3-10, T3-36).
relationships.display_finding: Benchmark scores rose only 34.35→34.75 and Likert scores 3.11→3.34, while the 200B checkpoint scored below the 197B checkpoint.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DENSE-CORE models at 350M and 1B parameters, and 350M/1B models trained for 100B or 200B tokens
reader_labels.reason: Aggregate downstream benchmark scores rise from 39.24 to 40.16 for the 350M DENSE-CORE run as tokens increase, and from 39.24 to 41.97 across 350M-to-1B at 100B tokens and 41.97 to 44.05 for the 1B run at 200B tokens (T3-05, T3-11, T3-15–T3-17). Instruction-tuning aggregates also rise for these conditions (T3-26–T3-27, T3-38–T3-39, T3-44–T3-47). These are downstream score improvements, not fitted predictions.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Data-regime comparisons at 350M and 100B total pretraining tokens
reader_labels.reason: Downstream aggregates vary with the data subset: AA HIGH scores below RANDOM on the pretraining suite, while several filtered subsets score above it; the study therefore does not show a data-independent scaling relation, and does not fit a predictive curve (T3-01–T3-09).
